newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar market quiet, mixed reaction on China.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar market quiet, mixed reaction on China.

text.p: Thai sugar market was quiet during the holiday season with Thai premiums unquoted in the market this week.
Thai traders were mixed on news that China will continue to limit sugar imports for 1997.

"I'm not worried by the report. First of all, the sugar imports for reprocessing are still allowed. Second, believe me, there will continue to be sugar smuggling in China," said a major Thai sugar exporter.
A trader at a Japanese house said there was no activity in the Thai market this week because of the holiday. "Therefore, premiums were unquoted," he said.
The January/March deliveries were bid around 0.70 cent per pound over New York while May/July was quoted around 0.45/0.55 cent per pound over New York futures last week.
At Thai ports, there were new declarations for January, mostly for deliveries to Japan as crushing in Thailand gathers steam.
